title: Startup Proof fails on main since wallet pin a083cea (runtime boot exceeds 30 s on the CI emulator)
description: Android API 36 Startup Proof has failed on every main run since the pin to seriouscoderone/fortweb a083cea (runs 53-60). Failure: 'FortWeb reported a fatal startup condition ... request_timeout method=vaults.list timeout_ms=30000', preceded by worker_invalidation reason='worker boot failed' (Runtime request timed out for worker boot). Passing run 51 (pin 4d40134): whole test took 26 s, so the emulator boots the runtime in about 20 s of a 30 s budget. Only startup difference on a fresh install in a083cea: the home route now renders the 'Starting your wallet...' page with an infinitely animated loading bar instead of the static splash. Emulator runs with -gpu swiftshader_indirect (software rendering). Hypothesis: the continuous 60 fps animation competes for CPU with the runtime boot and pushes it past 30 s.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed by experiment; fix has a regression test; Startup Proof green on main in CI.
notes:
2026-11-12 investigation. Evidence: run 60 logcat shows request_start vaults.list at 01:14:31.0, runtime_origin_contract_forwarded (worker alive) at 31.9, then nothing until worker_invalidation 'worker boot failed' at 01:15:01.1. Passing run 51 (pin 4d40134): 'Starting 1 tests' 19:39:50 -> 'Finished' 19:40:16, so boot took about 20 s. Emulator: 2 virtual cores (cpuinfo), -gpu swiftshader_indirect, and busy with first-boot system work during the window. a083cea did not touch runtime/bridge.ts; on a fresh install its only start-up change is the starting page with an infinite CSS animation (document.getAnimations() shows loading-bar-slide running, iterations infinite; the pre-existing page-fadein runs once). Not reproducible in headless desktop Chromium (5.48 s vs 5.50 s on 4 cores, 8.2 s vs 7.7 s on 1 core, within noise), so the emulator run is the test of the hypothesis. Fix: FortWeb 354f8f9 moves the bar on a 300 ms timer (4 positions, no animation or transition, timer stops when no bar shows, none under reduced motion); regression test in playwright/fortweb-fast-launch.spec.ts. Pinned in 704679d.
CI result for the 300 ms bar (pin 354f8f9, commit 704679d): Startup Proof run 61 PASSED, so removing the continuous animation fixes the timeout. But the test took 43.1 s; passing runs before the regression took 25.6-37.4 s (runs 38, 45, 46, 50, 51) and the failing runs 42.9-44.6 s, of which 30 s is the boot timeout. That puts the boot in run 61 at about 29 s of its 30 s budget on a slow runner (emulator boot 71 s). Each bar step is one drawn frame, so the bar was slowed to one step a second: FortWeb 47b10f4, pinned in 9a1be48.
Second sample of the 300 ms bar (dispatch run 62, fast runner): pass, test 32.1 s. One-step-a-second bar (pin 47b10f4, main 542d49d): Startup Proof run 63 PASSED with the test at 21.2 s, the fastest of all sampled runs (pre-regression passes: 25.6-37.4 s). All 10 workflows on 542d49d are green.
Correction: seven failed runs (53, 54, 56-60), not eight; runs 52 and 55 were cancelled by later pushes.
close_reason: Root cause confirmed on the CI emulator: the start page's infinite CSS animation drew a frame per refresh and starved the runtime boot (8 failing runs). Fix: the loading bar moves once a second on a timer, no animation (FortWeb 354f8f9 + 47b10f4, regression test in fortweb-fast-launch.spec.ts). Verified: Startup Proof run 63 green at 21.2 s; all 10 workflows green on main 542d49d.

title: iOS fork is 98 behind upstream; iOS shell trails the wallet and has a one-way bridge, so parity needs a sync, a CI health check, then a port of the 11 phone features
description: Established 2026-11-12 by reading both repositories. (1) seriouscoderone/fortios main (b43a0c8, 2026-05-01) is 98 commits behind keri-foundation/fortios main (c293f6a, 2026-10-05) and 0 ahead: syncing is a fast-forward. (2) The Foundation's iOS app pins FortWeb bdb81af (2026-09-09) with runtime source runtime-source-pyodide-314-20260909; FortWeb main has five later commits (#33, #38, #39, #40, #41) and Fortoid builds against main plus our fork commits with the newer hio-0.7.20 runtime source. Nobody has shown that today's wallet boots in the iOS shell. (3) The iOS bridge (KeriWallet/WebBridge.swift, WKScriptMessageHandler 'bridge', trusted origin app://local) is one-way: it cannot answer the page, so none of Fortoid's 11 native_request capabilities exist on iOS; the wallet's native-capabilities.ts only speaks to Android's window.bridge, and without a native side the wallet still runs with a passcode and hides fingerprint unlock and QR scanning. bridge-contract.json in the iOS repo is the shared source for bridge constants (generates Swift and Kotlin). (4) iOS CI (ios-security.yml, job swift-tests on macos-26) runs xcodebuild test on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.5; standard hosted runners are free on public repos, so iOS can be built and tested from a cloud session through CI. Deployment target iOS 16.4. (5) Camera QR, real Face ID and secure-chip keys need a physical iPhone; installing there means Xcode on the owner's Mac. Verdict: sync the fork and run a CI health check with our wallet now (cheap); port the 11 capabilities and the wallet's iOS transport after the first browser demonstration, so it is done once. Deferral is scheduling, not descope.

title: Converge the SAID/KERI P2P requirements (v2) with the browser vision
description:
Owner's other thread: Claude doc 'SAID / KERI P2P Architecture: Updated Requirements (v2)'. Analysis 2026-11-11: it is the data layer (schemas by SAID, ACDC write grants, encrypted records, mailbox sync, adoption manifests, percolated OOBI discovery); docs/vision/authentic-web-browser.md is the host layer (where apps run, consent, per-app AIDs, hardware unlock). Its 'request interface (sign, verify, encrypt, decrypt)' == the vision's KERI API.

Decisions the owner needs to make before a merged spec:
1. Domains: required of every adopter (P2P) vs people without domains (browser). Proposal: only organizations publish from domains; people signal adoption to peers they exchange with.
2. One identity per person on a multi-device multi-sig group (P2P) vs one AID per app/relationship (vision); KERI delegation would link them publicly.
3. Put the app's code bundle SAID in the adoption manifest so it doubles as the app manifest.
4. Bridge parity: 11 Android-only bridge calls exist (device, biometric, keystore x4, secret x4, qr); FortWeb's native client has no iOS transport; P2P requires iOS and Android together.
5. Phone limits: the Python engine only runs in the foreground with the vault unlocked, so scheduled re-signing/background refresh happen at next unlock.
Also open in that doc: should only signed manifests count as adoption (its comment thread).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Owner decides 1-5
- One merged spec (vision + P2P) in docs/, with a first build slice chosen
notes:
OWNER DECISIONS 2026-11-11 (voice, restated):
1. Domains: like the WWW, people need no domain. Organizations publish schemas at their domains (OOBIs). A person types a web address into the KERI browser; it reads the OOBIs there, loads/understands the schemas, and percolates outward (other referenced domains), possibly in the background, depth maybe a setting. Wallets are nodes.
2. Identity: multi-sig is NOT planned (advanced feature; Sam Smith: pre-rotation + signing keys are enough for normal people). The P2P doc oversold it. Multi-device identity therefore has no mechanism yet (open, not blocking).
3. Model: published schemas = a TYPE (an application's interface, 'what it means to be a candlestick maker'), not tied to an AID. A wallet INSTANTIATES a type as its own AID (e.g. my candlestick-maker AID for the wax company). Deployed SERVICES have service AIDs; an org may publish hundreds of types and run services for only some. 'Interoperability by default' = open invitation to instantiate roles. Apps brought into the browser + where app code comes from: owner will supply a separate application document; do not design it yet.
4. iOS: in scope, make iOS ready too. Owner has a Mac and iOS simulators. Fork exists: seriouscoderone/fortios (last pushed 2026-07-21, needs syncing with upstream).
5. Phone limits: must be overcome; KERI mailbox expected to let the wallet go online/offline.
STILL OPEN on domains (asked owner): (a) is a person's instantiation visible/counted by anyone (the org, the public, nobody)? (b) does an unsigned schema file count as adoption or only a manifest signed by the org's AID?
HOLD: do not merge the specs until the owner's application document arrives.
OWNER DECISIONS 2026-11-11 (second round, voice, restated):
6. Devices: NO shared identity across devices. Each wallet instance (desktop, phone, web) is separate with its own AIDs. Multi-sig stays an advanced feature, not developed further now. This CLOSES the 'one identity on desktop and phone' open item (P2P requirement 9 is dropped).
7. Device fit may belong in type definitions: e.g. an accounting role suits desktop (spreadsheet integration); field roles suit a phone (photos, barcode scanning). Idea to carry into the application spec: a type can state which wallet/capabilities it needs; Fortoid's capability bridge is the natural check.
8. A person's instantiation is PRIVATE: nobody is told or counts it. Others learn the role only when the person acts in it. Credentials/licences for a role are separate applications run by other independent actors (ACDCs), not part of instantiation.
9. Publishing a schema on a domain IS the organization's authorization (presence is the vote). No signing of schemas; no requirement for a signed manifest for it to count. My suggestion to count only signed manifests is withdrawn; this answers the open comment in the P2P doc (bare file counts).
10. Versioning: a changed type is a new schema that links back to the schema it supersedes (owner's application document will define this). Note: with SAIDs the link must live in the NEW schema pointing back; the old schema cannot be edited to point forward.
Domains questions are now fully answered. Still waiting for the owner's application document before merging specs.
2026-11-12: Owner supplied the application-language documents (from a private repository): definitions are models, authorizations and responsibilities; a runtime instantiates responsibilities; the workbench is where the work happens. Merged vision drafted as a PRIVATE document for the owner's review; nothing from those documents is committed to this public fork until the owner says it may be. Open rulings for the owner: (1) shared-data semantics: actor model vs shared workspace; (2) the published form of definitions (the bundled KERI library only checks that a document's $id is its own SAID at an OOBI address, so all definition kinds could be served that way; FortWeb's entry point still rejects such addresses); (3) one AID per role taken on; (4) what a person sees after taking on a role; (5) whether the merged vision may be public; (6) catching up from the mailbox on next open. The public docs/vision/authentic-web-browser.md is stale in two places (apps as signed code bundles; multi-sig research) and will be rewritten once (5) is answered.
OWNER RULINGS 2026-11-12 (voice, restated):
11. Shared data: each node (wallet, browser, service) keeps its own data in its own local database next to its KELs and TELs; KERI's own database is the standard choice, any other local store is allowed. So there is no shared workspace; the actor model governs and the P2P design is plumbing. Checked in code: the wallet's KERI store is the browser-safe interface over IndexedDB (keri.db.webdbing/webbasing, keri.app.webkeeping); native KERIpy uses LMDB (keri.db.dbing).
12. Published form: all kinds of definition are published the same way, in whatever file format the designer project settles on.
13. Roles: a role is a collection of ACDC credentials; the AID that holds them can perform it. (Corrects my earlier 'one AID per role' reading; one AID can hold several roles, and all credentials a role needs must be issued to the same AID.)
Also: the owner's public repository mad-discovery is the publication and discovery work; not read yet, not attached to this session.
Still open: default AID when taking on a role (new vs reuse); what a person sees after taking on a role; whether the merged vision may be public; mailbox catch-up on next open.
OWNER RULINGS 2026-11-12 (second round, restated):
14. Missing credentials do not block taking on a role: the wallet shows a warning. An AID acquires the credentials over time, like earning certifications; the processes and schemas for acquiring them are expected to be published in the application language too.
15. Publication and discovery: use the owner's public mad-discovery project where it is compatible; where it is not OOBI compatible, update it.
16. The owner asked to make the KERI forks private for now. This replaces the 'may the merged vision be public' question.
MAD-DISCOVERY ASSESSMENT (public repo, README and docs/design.md read in full at 359a13a):
- A source is a plain static folder: source.json + definitions/<SAID>.json + pages/. Its address is an https URL ending /source.json. Every definition is checked byte for byte against its SAID (Blake3-256). Publications are unsigned offerings; a reader walks introductions from source to source. This supersedes the P2P design's /oobi/<SAID> publication paths and signed manifest, and matches rulings 9 and 12.
- Identity side is OOBI compatible: source.json may state 'by' (an AID) and 'oobi', which the wallet's existing OOBI resolver can resolve. The live test source (mad.seriouscoder.one: 3 publications, 26 served definitions) states neither yet.
- Definitions are NOT resolvable by the bundled KERI library as data OOBIs: it only fetches /oobi/<SAID> at the host root and checks a schema by $id, while a source serves definitions/<SAID>.json and the test definitions carry the SAID in 'd'. This matters only where a definition is used as an ACDC schema; mad-discovery's design already lists a keripy-shaped /oobi/<SAID> as a possible later extra.
- Two gaps for a wallet in a browser/WebView: the live source sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header (checked with an Origin header), so a page cannot fetch it; and the reader's fetch routine is Node-only (session.ts imports fetchJson from fetch.ts).
- Proposed updates, awaiting the owner: (a) sources send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (alternative: the wallet fetches through a native bridge capability); (b) make the fetch routine injectable so the SAID check and the walk run in a browser; (c) optional /oobi/<SAID> copies, with the SAID in $id, for definitions used as ACDC schemas.
- First demonstration now targets the live test source: address box in the wallet -> read source.json -> list publications -> verify definitions -> take on a role, with a warning per missing credential.
PRIVACY FINDINGS (GitHub docs read 2026-11-12):
- A fork's visibility cannot be changed. Route: Settings > General > Danger Zone > Leave fork network (fork must be public, under 1 GB, no child forks; permanent), then change visibility to private. Git history is kept; the docs say issues, pull requests, stars, watchers and comments of the fork are not retained, and do not say what happens to a pull request the fork has open upstream (keri-foundation/fortweb#49). Alternative: bare clone, delete the fork, recreate it, mirror push; the docs warn that deleting a fork permanently deletes associated pull requests.
- Private repositories pay for Actions from the plan's included amount ($12 Free, $18 Pro; about 2,000 or 3,000 Linux minutes a month). One push to Fortoid main runs 10 workflows, about 43 billed minutes (measured on run 60), so roughly 46 pushes a month on Free. CI needs trimming before going private (emulator proofs manual or scheduled).
- If FortWeb goes private, Fortoid CI can no longer check it out (.github/actions/prepare-fortweb-runtime uses Fortoid's own token). The Demo APK step is continue-on-error, so the APK would ship WITHOUT the wallet and the proofs would fail. Needs a read-only deploy key or fine-grained token for FortWeb stored as a Fortoid Actions secret, and the checkout step wired to use it.
- The demo-latest APK on a private repository downloads only from a browser signed in to GitHub.
- This session cannot change repository settings; the owner does it.
17. 2026-11-12 (later): the owner dropped the privacy request after hearing what it takes ('Don't worry about making it private then'). The forks stay public. Consequence: material from the owner's private repositories stays out of these forks; the merged vision stays in the owner's private document until the owner says it may be published. The privacy findings above are kept for reference.

title: Faster launch: fingerprint prompt immediately + loading bar
description:
Owner on phone: ~3-4 s before the fingerprint prompt at launch. Likely cause: the default vault is known only after the Python runtime boots (vaults.list). Idea: remember the default vault's id/alias/createdAt locally after each launch, render its unlock screen and start the fingerprint prompt immediately, and open the vault as soon as the runtime is ready.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Cause measured (boot timeline from logs)
- Fingerprint prompt appears without waiting for runtime boot when the default vault has fingerprint unlock
notes: Plan: (1) launch-cache.ts remembers {id, alias, createdAt, storageName, otpConfigured} of the default vault (non-secret) after each vaults.list. (2) At launch before vaults load: home -> cached vault's unlock; findVault falls back to the cached record so the unlock page renders and its fingerprint prompt runs while Pyodide boots; vaults.open queues until the worker is ready. (3) When vaults load: don't re-render the cached unlock page (no double prompt); if the cached vault no longer exists, clear the cache and re-run launch routing. (4) Loading UI: indeterminate bar + 'Starting your wallet...' while the runtime boots; bar on the unlock card while opening. Tests: real runtime with delayed boot + fake bridge whose secret store persists in localStorage.

title: Review: Foundation 'contexts' preview (fortweb#47) vs piece C
description:
fortweb#47 (Nov 8, fixture-only, not wired in): 'Locksmith' flow where a context = a part of life (work/family) kept separate to reduce linkability; chosen at credential presentation time ('Present using Family'); first-use creates first context. Undefined: whether a context is a vault, an identifier, or a label. Locksmith (keri-foundation/locksmith, Qt desktop wallet) has no product 'contexts' or default vault yet. Implication for C: C's 'open straight into the wallet' is orthogonal to contexts (contexts are chosen when presenting, not when opening). Open question for owner: map context -> vault or context -> group inside one wallet.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Owner picks a mapping before C is planned
notes: Context=one AID check: fortweb#42 ipex.present takes a single presenterAid, which must be a local identifier and the credential's recipientAid. So 'Present using <context>' resolves to exactly one local AID; consistent with context=AID. Against a pure rename: #47 copy still says 'presentations can use different identifiers or credentials', keeping 'identifiers' as a separate word, so contexts may later span several AIDs (e.g. pairwise). 'Family' in the mock is the user's own family-life persona, not relatives (relatives are remotes).
